title: Fix Product Name Format
statement:
A shop logs every sale in one table, but its product names were typed by hand:

- `Sales(sale_id, product_name, sale_date)`: one row per sale; `sale_id` is unique. `product_name` may have extra spaces before or after it and may mix upper and lower case, so `'  LcPhOnE'` and `'LCPHONE '` are the same product. `sale_date` is the day of the sale.

Clean every name by removing its leading and trailing spaces and turning it into lower case (spaces inside a name are kept, so `'LC Phone'` and `'LCPhone'` stay different products). Then count the sales of each cleaned product in each calendar month.

Report one row per product and month with at least one sale, with the columns `product_name` (the cleaned name), `sale_date` (the month as the text `'YYYY-MM'`) and `total` (how many sales it had that month). Order the rows by `product_name` ascending, then by `sale_date` ascending.
constraints: product_name may have leading or trailing spaces and any letter case
reference:
WITH cleaned AS (
  SELECT LOWER(TRIM(product_name)) AS product_name,
         DATE_FORMAT(sale_date, '%Y-%m') AS sale_date
  FROM Sales
)
SELECT product_name, sale_date, COUNT(*) AS total
FROM cleaned
GROUP BY product_name, sale_date
ORDER BY product_name, sale_date;
brute:
SELECT DISTINCT LOWER(TRIM(product_name)) AS product_name,
       LEFT(sale_date, 7) AS sale_date,
       COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY LOWER(TRIM(product_name)), LEFT(sale_date, 7)) AS total
FROM Sales
ORDER BY product_name, sale_date
notes:
## Intuition

Two spellings belong to the same product when they agree after the noise is stripped away: drop the spaces at the ends and ignore letter case. Likewise, two dates belong to the same month when their `'YYYY-MM'` prefixes agree. Once every row is rewritten into that clean form, the task is an ordinary count per (product, month) group.

## Approach

1. The CTE `cleaned` rewrites every sale: `LOWER(TRIM(product_name))` gives the clean name and `DATE_FORMAT(sale_date, '%Y-%m')` gives the month.
2. Read from `cleaned` and `GROUP BY product_name, sale_date`, so each group is one product in one month.
3. `COUNT(*) AS total` counts the sales in each group.
4. `ORDER BY product_name, sale_date` sorts by name, then month.

## Example 1, step by step

`cleaned` turns the six sales into:

| product_name | sale_date |
| --- | --- |
| lcphone | 2000-01 |
| lcphone | 2000-01 |
| lcphone | 2000-02 |
| lckeychain | 2000-02 |
| lckeychain | 2000-02 |
| matryoshka | 2000-03 |

Grouping gives (lckeychain, 2000-02) with 2 sales, (lcphone, 2000-01) with 2, (lcphone, 2000-02) with 1 and (matryoshka, 2000-03) with 1, already in the required order.

## Complexity

- Time: O(S log S) for S sales, dominated by grouping and sorting.
- Space: O(S) for the cleaned rows and the groups.

## Pitfalls

- Forgetting `TRIM` leaves `'  lcphone'` and `'lcphone'` as separate products, and reports names with spaces.
- Grouping by `MONTH(sale_date)` alone merges January 2000 with January 2001; the year must be part of the key.
- In MySQL, `GROUP BY product_name` in the same `SELECT` that defines the alias `product_name` groups by the raw column, not the cleaned one; cleaning in a CTE first removes that ambiguity.
- `TRIM` removes only the ends: `'lc phone'` keeps its inner space and is a different product from `'lcphone'`.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `cleaned` | one row per sale with the clean name and its `'YYYY-MM'` month |
| `product_name` | the trimmed, lower-case name |
| `sale_date` | the month of the sale, as text |
| `total` | number of sales of that product in that month |

narration.1: The CTE cleaned rewrites every sale into a canonical form before anything is counted.
narration.2: Trim the spaces at both ends and lower-case the name, so all spellings of a product agree.
narration.3: Keep only the year and month of the sale date, as YYYY-MM text.
narration.6: Report each product and month with the number of sales in it.
narration.8: Each group is one cleaned product in one month.
narration.9: Sort by name first, then by month.
